course_name: Fundamentals of Programming. Part 2. Programming Methodologies

course_profile.one_sentence_summary: A foundational course focusing on object-oriented programming methodologies, advanced C# features, and complex data structures.
course_profile.short_summary: This course covers the theoretical and methodological foundations of object-oriented programming using C# and the .NET framework. Students explore classes, inheritance, polymorphism, interfaces, exception handling, delegates, LINQ, and custom data structures like trees and linked lists. Practical skills are enforced through automated coding labs and Git version control.

source_coverage.coverage_comment: Extraction is based on the official syllabus (Силабус) from Kyiv Polytechnic Institute, which includes detailed lecture topics, lab assignments, and assessment criteria[cite: 5, 105, 118].

theoretical_understanding: Understand the paradigms of object-oriented and procedural programming[cite: 44].
Comprehend the C# type system, memory management, stack vs heap, and .NET garbage collection[cite: 49].
Understand the concepts of inheritance, early/late binding, and polymorphism[cite: 53, 55].
practical_implementation: Implement classes, interfaces, and class hierarchies in C#[cite: 45, 59].
Develop programs utilizing exception handling mechanisms (try, catch, finally, throw)[cite: 62].
Implement linear and non-linear data structures including linked lists, stacks, queues, and binary search trees[cite: 70, 72].
Write LINQ queries to filter, sort, and group data collections[cite: 67, 124].
analysis_validation: Test and validate code through the Autocode automated verification platform[cite: 118, 154].
Analyze the stack trace of exceptions during debugging[cite: 63, 130].
architecture_design: Design software models establishing appropriate relationships between classes (aggregation, composition, inheritance, realization)[cite: 60].
Choose appropriate built-in .NET Generic Collections for specific algorithmic requirements[cite: 73].
research_and_prototyping: Self-study and experiment with dynamic LINQ and expression trees[cite: 133].
Explore the implementation of hash table collisions and highly branched/threaded trees[cite: 133].

lab_formats: Automated coding assignments checked via Autocode system [cite: 153]
Manual defense of the implemented laboratory work [cite: 148]
expected_artifacts: Source code commits pushed to a global Git repository (autocode.git.epam.com) [cite: 115]
implementation_tasks: Write functions and use different parameter passing methods [cite: 123]
Design and use C# classes with constructors and properties [cite: 118]
Implement single inheritance and virtual functions to achieve polymorphism [cite: 123]
Handle errors using custom and standard exceptions [cite: 124]
Construct custom data structures and use .NET generic collections [cite: 118, 124]
engineering_practices: Continuous Assessment / Automated Testing via Autocode [cite: 118, 154]

curricular_relations.reason: Procedural concepts like basic functions and logic flow are required to understand method implementation within OOP structures[cite: 38].
Understanding basic algorithms is necessary for implementing operations (insertion, deletion, traversal) on complex data structures like binary search trees[cite: 38, 72].
The principles of OOP are directly applied and realized using the C# programming language syntax[cite: 12].
A solid grasp of C# fundamentals, including lambda expressions and delegates, is a prerequisite for utilizing LINQ effectively[cite: 66, 67].

what_student_can_understand: The theoretical foundations of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)[cite: 12].
How memory is managed in .NET via the stack, heap, and garbage collector[cite: 49].
The mechanics of early and late binding, inheritance, and polymorphism[cite: 55].
what_student_can_build: C# applications structured around robust class hierarchies and interfaces[cite: 45, 59].
Custom implementations of lists, queues, stacks, and binary search trees[cite: 70, 72].
Systems that safely handle execution errors using exception blocks[cite: 62].
what_student_can_apply: LINQ expressions to query and manipulate collections of data in-memory[cite: 67].
Delegates and events for handling asynchronous or event-driven actions[cite: 66].
Git version control for submitting code via the Autocode system[cite: 115].
